one_liner: Full build system combining object caching, unity builds and distributed compilation; replaces make/MSBuild, not a wrapper.
what_it_does: FASTBuild is a standalone build system (the `fbuild` executable) driven by its own BFF description language, so it replaces an existing build tool (make, MSBuild, Ninja) rather than wrapping it. It bundles three speed techniques in one tool: automatic Unity/Blob builds, a local or network object cache, and distributed compilation across worker machines running FBuildWorker. It targets PC, Mac, Linux, consoles and mobile game/engine builds using MSVC, GCC, Clang, SNC, GreenHills, CodeWarrior or NVCC.
how_it_is_fast: Unity/Blob builds merge many .cpp files into fewer translation units, cutting per-file compiler startup/parse overhead. The object cache stores compiled objects keyed by build inputs and reuses them across machines instead of recompiling identical code. Distributed compilation preprocesses source locally then ships it to idle worker machines running FBuildWorker, so object compilation runs in parallel across a farm rather than being limited to one machine's core count.
when_to_use: Large multi-platform (PC/console/mobile) C/C++ game or engine codebase, where you're willing to author the build in FASTBuild's own BFF language
Team has spare workstation or render-farm capacity to run FBuildWorker for network distribution
CI or local dev with deterministic compiler output, where object-cache hits repeat across builds and machines
Cross-compiler shop needing one build tool across MSVC, GCC, Clang, SNC, GreenHills, CodeWarrior, NVCC
Want unity-build automation without hand-writing jumbo .cpp generation scripts
when_not_to_use: Want to keep an existing CMake/Make/MSBuild/Ninja build and just add caching or distribution without rewriting build files
No dedicated worker machines or spare network compute — distributed mode adds nothing without hardware to distribute to

Non-deterministic compiler output or unusual toolchains: issue #1021 (cache errors when system locale differs) and #992 (clang-cl PCH + cache 'fatal error in some situations') show real cache-correctness edge cases
Linux build farm with >32 cores per worker: issue #1197 reports the CPU-affinity mask is 32-bit, giving a wrong mask on wider machines
Small or single-machine project where compile time is already short — BFF authoring and cache/worker setup cost may not pay off

integration.dependencies: none documented for the core build; the OSUI component links native OS UI frameworks (WinAPI on Windows, Cocoa .mm files on macOS)
integration.min_toolchain: not documented as a stated minimum; Linux CI (Linux.yml) builds and tests with GCC 10 and Clang 15 on Ubuntu 22.04 — Windows/macOS minimum compiler versions not checked this session
integration.platforms: Windows, Linux and macOS as build hosts (README); used to target PC, Mac, Linux, consoles, smartphones and retro systems as build outputs — specific host CPU architectures not documented
integration.thread_safety: not documented — FASTBuild is a standalone CLI/executable build tool, not an embeddable library, so this doesn't apply in the usual sense
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: false — requires authoring or converting your build description into FASTBuild's own BFF language; it is not a wrapper around an existing make/CMake/MSBuild setup

gotchas: Cache correctness assumes deterministic compiler output; issue #1021 shows cache errors when the system locale differs and #992 shows clang-cl PCH + cache producing a fatal error in some situations
Distributed compilation is reported to intermittently fail (issue #1058, open, 'Need More Info')
Linux CPU-affinity helper uses a 32-bit mask (issue #1197), so it can compute the wrong core mask on machines with more than 32 cores
GitHub's UI reports 'no license' for this repo because the license file lives at Code/LICENSE.TXT rather than repo root, even though it is zlib-licensed
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick FASTBuild when you're building (or willing to rebuild) a multi-platform C/C++ project around its own BFF language and want unity builds, object cache and worker-farm distribution bundled in one tool. Pick NativeLink or HOMCC instead when you need to keep an existing Bazel/REAPI or distcc-compatible build and only add remote caching or distributed compilation without rewriting build files, or octobuild when the target is specifically Unreal Engine's UBT/UAT pipeline.
verified_claims_summary: fastbuild.org's features page gives first-party, unqualified figures — object caching 'up to 10x', Unity/Blob builds 'improvements of 10x or more', distributed compilation 'speedups of 5x are common' — each measured against the same build without that FASTBuild feature enabled. No workload, hardware, compiler, or flags are given, so these are vendor round numbers, not a reproducible benchmark.
status_note: Actively maintained — the dev branch (where patches land) was last committed 2026-09-20, days before this entry — and zlib-licensed (Code/LICENSE.TXT), so it's free to vendor; its 1.4k GitHub stars understate real usage since it's mainly distributed via fastbuild.org binaries and used by many closed-source game studios.
